DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung's Disease

The X-ray findings of dilated bowel loops with no rectal gas, combined with bilious vomiting and failure to pass meconium, strongly suggest a distal intestinal obstruction. Given the infant's age and specific symptoms, Hirschsprung's disease is the most likely diagnosis, although a distal atresia must also be considered.
